subject: Discovery recap: unit economics, feature-level tokenization, and next milestones
snippet: Recap of token volumes, budget range and a starter $/1M suggestion + next steps.
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@medworks.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: token volumes, budget bracket, and follow ups

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for a great call today. Quick recap to lock in what we heard and lay out the next steps so we can put a crisp econ model together for your team.

What we heard (confirm / correct):
- Priority features: 1) Patient visit summarization (clinical summaries), 2) Triage/chatbot, 3) Discharge note generation.
- Rough monthly token estimates (you said ballpark): summarization ~600M, triage ~250M, discharge notes ~150M — total ~1.0B tokens/month.
- Budget range under consideration: $20k–$45k/month for inference (you mentioned finance is comfortable in that window for a pilot).
- Key commercial asks: target $/1M tokens target (finance), unit $/feature estimates (PM), CAC payback horizon (growth/exec).

I sketched an initial approach below so we can iterate quickly:
1) Ask from your side (deliver by EOD Fri if possible):
   - Confirm the monthly usage numbers by feature (CSV or small spreadsheet).
   - Any SLO constraints (p99 latency <400ms for triage?).
   - Target gross margin or acceptable vendor markup for procurement (if you have a guide).
2) What we’ll deliver:
   - A one-page unit-econ break-out showing $/1M token sensitivity (three price bands) and resulting $/feature, plus CAC payback scenarios given your LTV and expected conversion rates.
   - A recommended pilot config (model family + quantization/batch settings) and expected throughput/latency trade-offs.

Preliminary numbers (very rough, for discussion):
- Redwood internal inference cost assumption (estimate for pilot): ~$6.00 per 1M tokens (this is our backend execution cost estimate including infra & ops amortization).
- Target gross margin band: 55–70% (varies by contract term).
- Price -> implied $/1M tokens: at 60% gross margin, price = cost / (1 - 0.60) => $6 / 0.40 = $15.00 per 1M tokens. At 65% margin => ~$17.14/1M.

Using the 1.0B token/month example:
- At $15/1M => monthly spend = 1000 * $15 = $15,000/month.
- At $17.14/1M => monthly spend = 1000 * $17.14 = $17,140/month.
- Note: those sits under your lower-bound budget; we can also show a premium tier (faster model / higher SLA) at ~$30/1M which yields $30k/month.

$ per feature (example using $17.14/1M):
- Summarization (600M): 600 * $17.14 = $10,284/month -> $/feature (per summary) = depends on summaries/month; if ~300k summaries => $10,284 / 300k ~ $0.034 per summary.
- Triage chatbot (250M): 250 * $17.14 = $4,285/month -> per convo if 125k convos => $0.034 per convo.
- Discharge notes (150M): 150 * $17.14 = $2,571/month -> per note if 12k notes => $0.214 per note.

CAC payback (quick sketch):
- If average feature revenue per user (NAR) = $X and conversion from trial to paid = Y, we’ll map that against the incremental inference cost per paid user to estimate months-to-payback. We need your average revenue per user and expected conversion rates to finish this.

Next steps / timeline:
- Priya: confirm the per-feature monthly token CSV + any SLA callouts by EOD Friday (6/22).
- Diego/Marissa: produce 1-pager unit-econ + 3 price bands by Tue 6/25; include sensitivity table and 2 pilot configs.
- Ben: prep a short internal pricing note for procurement cadence.

If that all sounds right I’ll draft the one-pager and attach the modeling workbook for you to review.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@medworks.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: token volumes, budget bracket, and follow ups

Thanks Diego — the recap is accurate. A few clarifications and an attachment (exported estimates):
- Confirmed monthly tokens by feature (attached medworks_token_estimates.xlsx):
  * Summarization: 600M (we calculate summaries generated per encounter; see sheet)
  * Triage/chat: 250M
  * Discharge notes: 150M
  * Total: ~1,000M/month (1.0B)
- Budget: finance is comfortable with a pilot up to $40k/mo if the productizing roadmap (3 months) shows clear unit economics and a path to 6–9 month CAC payback.
- Latency: triage must be <500ms p95 for most flows; some deeper follow-ups can be async.
- Procurement timeline: they’ll want an initial pilot PO and then a 6–12 month contract if pilot targets are met. For PO we need a rate-card and expected monthly cap.

I’ve looped Samir (ops) and procurement (procure@medworks.ai) on this thread so they have the estimates.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Product, MedWorks Health
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@medworks.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: token volumes, budget bracket, and follow ups

Great — thanks for the file and the procurement timeline. Based on the clarified target ($40k/mo pilot cap and p95 latency target), here’s a tightened set of recommendations I’ll include in the one-pager:

1) Price banding (starter):
   - Conservative price band (term & pilot discount): $14–$18 per 1M tokens (implied gross margin ~57–66% if cost is $6/1M). At $16/1M midpoint, ~ $16k/month for 1B tokens.
   - Standard enterprise band: $18–$22 per 1M tokens (for SLA + support), ~ $18k–$22k/month for 1B tokens.
   - Premium SLA (faster model, priority capacity): $28–$34 per 1M tokens (for up to $34k/month).

2) Pilot recommendation: start with the conservative starter config (quantized 8-bit model family + dynamic batching) to validate quality/throughput. If triage latency metrics are missed, step up to the standard enterprise band model.

3) Unit economics output I will attach: a detailed workbook showing per-feature $/1M sensitivity and two CAC-payback scenarios (base conversion and high conversion).

4) For procurement: we’ll provide a simple rate-card with monthly cap options (20k / 30k / 40k) and a sample PO template.

Ben — can you pull a stub rate-card and an initial SOW draft so I can attach them to the one-pager? Aim for something we can hand to procure@medworks.ai next week.

Priya — expect the one-pager and workbook by Tue 6/25 as discussed.

Thanks,
Diego
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: token volumes, budget bracket, and follow ups

On it — I’ll draft the rate-card + SOW stub today and attach the initial_inference_pricing_model.xlsx. I’ll keep the pricing bands Diego suggested and add an annual/commitment discount option for their procurement team to evaluate.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
